text:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-p95+p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate (hosted-us-west). p95 from 180ms -> 810ms, p99 from 1.2s -> 3.9s. SLO risk. paging oncall(sara-oncall). :rotating_light:

sara-oncall: I got paged. jumping in. what customers affected?

henry-support: Seeing elevated error-rate on a few enterprise accounts, partial streaming stalls reported by customer-a and customer-b. Support ticket ids: #2341, #2342. No immediate data exfil.

amir-runtime: looking at the runtime dashboard now. Streaming stalls metric shows spike in 'streaming-chunk-latency' and 'kv-cache-miss-rate' around 12:13 UTC. Kernel queue length on a subset of pods increased.

kai-eng: any deploys around that time?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Completed rollout redwood-large-v2 @ 12:05 UTC to pool-us-west-1 (65 pods).

sara-oncall: hmm deploy ~8 minutes before spike. Amir can you correlate pods that got the new image?

amir-runtime: running quick cluster query: `kubectl get pods -l app=runtime -o wide --sort-by=.status.startTime` then `kubectl logs` for suspicious pods. Initial grep: 7 pods restarted between 12:03-12:07.

amir-runtime: paste: ```
# sample
Pod runtime-65a2  -> OOMKilled
Pod runtime-65b7  -> Restarted: CrashLoopBackOff
Pod runtime-66c1  -> Running
```

kai-eng: OOMs could cause increased queuing as requests shift. Are we seeing GPU memory pressure?

amir-runtime: nvidia-smi snapshots show some pods hitting 98% GPU mem. Also noticed a new kernel error in dmesg on one node about 'nv_link recovery' — possible driver flakiness.

sara-oncall: immediate mitigations we can do now?

amir-runtime: 1) take the suspect nodes out of rotation (cordon + drain) 2) scale up pool-us-west-1 by +6 nodes 3) enable canary fallback routing to redwood-medium-v1-quant for 15% traffic 4) temporarily reduce batch size for realtime route to 64 -> 32.

kai-eng: I'll start the node scale and cordon. Sara, want me to enable the routing fallback or do you want product signoff?

sara-oncall: do it. we need to reduce customer impact. Kai proceed with cordon/drain and scaling. Amir, do the routing change and batch config hotpatch.

amir-runtime: doing the routing change: `redwoodctl routing set /v1/generate --fallback redwood-medium-v1-quant --percent 15 --duration 15m`

amir-runtime: done. also pushed reduced batch override to the route.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Started node-scale request: pool-us-west-1 +6 -> provisioning.

henry-support: I've informed the two impacted customers that we're investigating and applied the temporary quality fallback. They report partial improvement on one stream.

lisa-product: Are any canary failures or obvious degradation in output quality? we should track eval regressions.

amir-runtime: enable quick evals on representative prompts: running 100-sample check on medium-quant vs large-v2. baseline p95 inner-latency results incoming.

amir-runtime: quick numbers: baseline large-v2 pre-spike p95 ~ 180ms, current large-v2 p95 ~ 820ms. medium-quant p95 ~ 420ms. quality diffs are minor for chat-style prompts; we'll log for product.

sara-oncall: status update in 10. current plan: cordon + drain suspected nodes, scale pool, keep fallback at 15% while we monitor latency. If p99 remains >2.5s we escalate to full roll-back of v2.

(6m later)

amir-runtime: cordon/drain completed on 3 suspect nodes; node-scale completed +4 nodes (2 still provisioning). p95 overall down to 330ms, p99 1.8s. streaming-stall alerts reduced by ~60%.

sara-oncall: good progress. hold fallback at 10% for now and keep batch smaller. Kai please watch autoscaler.

kai-eng: autoscaler stable. No further restarts on drained nodes. We'll keep nodes cordoned until postmortem.

henry-support: Customer-a says their streaming session recovered and resumed; Customer-b still sees intermittent chunk delays but improved. I've kept tickets updated.

lisa-product: please capture a sample prompt set for evals, and create a light quality regression alert if medium-quant differs >5% from baseline on key metrics.

amir-runtime: created quick-eval run id `eval-176834` and saved diffs to /reports/176834-eval.csv.

sara-oncall: decision log: short-term mitigation = scale + cordon + 10% fallback to medium-quant + reduce batch. No full rollback yet. Assign action items for incident review.

Assignments:
- amir-runtime: collect logs from OOM pods, nv driver dmesg, and GPU telemetry (action: upload to incident doc)
- kai-eng: keep nodes cordoned, follow up with infra to repro driver issue (action: infra ticket)
- henry-support: keep customers updated, escalate if any regression in last 30m
- lisa-product: run regression eval and flag quality incidents (action: create PR if threshold exceeded)
- sara-oncall: incident lead, run postmortem pipeline after stable and close incident when SLO stabilized.

(20m after start)

amir-runtime: full follow-up: p95 settled ~210ms, p99 ~650ms across the fleet. Fallback disabled at 14:05 UTC, batch reverts at 14:07 UTC. No further OOMs.

sara-oncall: marking incident as mitigated. Creating incident timeline + severity classification (S1 - SLO exposure). Will schedule postmortem.

henry-support: customers notified of mitigation and follow-up. No active customer escalations.

sara-oncall: quick root-cause hypothesis: new runtime image had an interaction with updated GPU driver causing occasional memory accounting mismatch -> OOMKills -> request queuing and tail latency. Need full repro and fix.

kai-eng: opened infra ticket #INF-712 with driver team and uploaded logs. We'll also add an automated pre-rollout smoke test for GPU mem pressure.

amir-runtime: saving full incident artifacts to /incidents/1768345678/artifacts (logs, eval CSVs, dashboard snapshots).

sara-oncall: thank you team. final checklist before close: postmortem draft by EOD tomorrow, action items assigned, customer comms wrap-up. I'll close the channel when done. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident severity: S1 (SLO exposure).
